question.text: The distance between the point <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and the point of intersection of the line <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> with the plane <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> is <math><mn>13</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then <math><mi>t</mi></math> equals to

solution.text:
Any point on the line is 3r+2, 4r –1, 12r+2
If it lies on the given plane, then 3r+2-4r-1+12r+2=5
⇒ 11r=0 ⇒ r=0
∴  Co-ordinates of the point of intersection of the given line and given plane are 2, -1, 2 and thus the required distance is 2+12+-1+52+2+102=13

⇒13=13t ⇒ t=1
